newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Chirac urges respect, national interest.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac urges respect, national interest.

text.p: Conservative French President Jacques Chirac told the first meeting of a left-wing cabinet on Thursday he hoped their power-sharing would be respectful and uphold the national interest.

"Here we are in a new period of 'cohabitation'. I do not doubt that it will take place in a dignified manner with mutual respect and a constant concern for France's interests," Chirac said at a brief meeting with the broad-left government headed by Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin.

Flanked by Martine Aubry, superminister for employment and social solidarity, and Education Minister Claude Allegre, Chirac sat with a fixed smile opposite Jospin at the oval cabinet table, with two Communist ministers also in the room.
"France has spoken. It has elected a new majority. You are the government resulting from this majority," Chirac was quoted as saying by the presidential press service.
The new cabinet posed together for photographers on the steps of the presidential palace after the 40-minute meeting, but Chirac stayed indoors did not take part in the group photo.

Ministers said the atmosphere was cordial at the cabinet meeting. Chirac's centre-right coalition was routed in last Sunday's parliamentary election, leaving him to suffer France's third period of left-right "cohabitation" in 11 years.
